fix: appointed Parmenion and Morcus
reason: Greek Μόρκον is the Illyrian Morcus, not Roman Marcus; matches ch. 11.

fix: He also persuaded the Rhodians to join in the war.
reason: Subject of ἔπεισε is Perseus, not the embassy; aorist clashes with Rhodian peace moves (ch. 10–11). Possibly conative/corrupt; translator decides.

fix: and then, when he came close to the wall at Demetrias, [...] spoke first with Menecrates and then with Antimachus [...]
reason: Two lacunae (after τῷ τείχει and after Ἀντιμάχῳ) smoothed over; mark with project convention [...].

fix: And the fact that Herophon [...] twice went as an envoy from Perseus to Eumenes
reason: Lacuna between Ἡροφῶν and ἐπρέσβευσε; mark [...] without other changes.

fix: Accordingly, Perseus, in his dealings with the Gauls and with Gentius, [...]
reason: Predicate lost in lacuna; 'were of a piece with this' is invented. ἀκολούθως τούτοις kept as 'Accordingly'.

fix: [as is set down in the section on public speeches]
reason: Bracketed excerptor's cross-reference (Constantinian 'On Speeches'), not Polybius' first person. Editor may prefer deleting it or a note.

fix: When Parmenion and Morcus, the envoys from Gentius, and with them Metrodorus, arrived at Rhodes
reason: Parmenion and Morcus are Gentius' envoys, not a separate group; Metrodorus accompanies them.

fix: the number of cavalry that had been lost, and [...] Gentius’ defection crushed them
reason: Lacuna before ἡ τοῦ Γενθίου μετάθεσις; mark [...], keep 'defection'.

fix: no one could adequately describe how far they work these up, given their lack of real material
reason: Greek says their elaboration is beyond description; English inverted it into 'inadequate, if at all'.

fix: for instance if [...] I should seem to use the same material, the same handling of events, or the same expressions
reason: τοῖς αὐτοῖς = repetition, not inconsistency; damaged text after οἷον εἰ marked [...].

fix: if I should anywhere make slips in the names of mountains or rivers or in the particular features of places
reason: παραπίπτωμεν = err; 'slip in' reads as 'insert'; τόπων ἰδιότησι = features of places.

fix: the siege of Phanoteia or Coroneia or [...]
reason: Third name survives only as ...ε...οῦ; 'Haliartus' is conjecture, not clearly recoverable. Translator may keep it flagged as conjecture.

fix: and beyond that [...] to dwell on the capture of Tarentum, Corinth, Sardis, Gaza, Bactra, and, above all, Carthage
reason: Lacuna after πρὸς δὲ τούτοις; mark [...]. Bracketed [πολιορκίαν] is an editorial supplement, needs no rendering.

fix: [...] Again, other writers on the Syrian war.
reason: Fragment opens with a lacuna and has no verb; 'have gone on at length' is supplied.

fix: the rumor prevailed among the multitude, in the time of Perseus the Macedonian, that it signified the eclipse of a king
reason: Μακεδόνος is singular (Perseus the Macedonian); παρὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς = the many generally; 'a king', not 'the king himself'.

fix: pretending that he was sacrificing to Heracles, a god who does not accept cowardly offerings from cowards or fulfill unlawful prayers
reason: Participles agree with Ἡρακλεῖ and are negated; English made the rites 'fitting'. American spelling per text.

fix: while encamped in Thessaly for almost two years [...].
reason: Lacuna (* **) after ἐπὶ δύ᾽ ἐνιαυτοὺς; mark with [...].

fix: For even so, a man can hardly show himself moderate in times of prosperity.
reason: καὶ γὰρ οὕτω μόλις = 'even so, scarcely'; English inverted to 'only in that way'.

fix: because she has lent these blessings to them too
reason: κέχρηκεν from χράω 'lend': Fortune has only lent the goods, until she decides otherwise.

fix: with Lycortas as commander of the whole allied force and Polybius of the cavalry
reason: ἡγεμόνα τῆς ὅλης συμμαχίας = commander of the whole force, not the infantry.
Not a lacuna: chapter seam. Ch. 24 Greek opens 'Μακεδονίᾳ ποιουμένου', so 'Macedonia' is correct.

fix: that Alexandria and the whole of Egypt, though brought to the last extremity, were set upright again, simply because the affairs of Perseus had already been decided
reason: English drops 'last extremity' and 'set upright again' and misreads φθάσαι κριθέντα as a decision about Perseus.
